(&#8220;Xilinx&#8221;). Prior to joining AMD, Mr.&#160;Peng served as the President and Chief Executive Officer of Xilinx. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial;font-weight:bold" id="toc425773_26">Executive Summary </p> <p style="margin-top:3pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">2022 Business Highlights </span></p> <p style="margin-top:3pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">2022 was a strong year for AMD as we navigated the challenging macro environment to deliver <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">best-in-class</span></span> growth and record profitability driven by our Embedded and Data Center segments. We had record annual revenue, record annual profitability and returned $3.7&#160;billion of cash to stockholders through share repurchases, despite the deterioration of our gaming graphics and PC businesses in the second half of the year. We closed our acquisitions of Xilinx, Inc. (&#8220;Xilinx&#8221;) and Pensando Systems Inc. (&#8220;Pensando&#8221;), which have strengthened our financial model and significantly diversified our business. Our Data Center and Embedded product sales grew from $3.9&#160;billion in 2021 to $10.6&#160;billion in 2022. In addition, we are seeing substantial new revenue synergy opportunities as we combine Xilinx&#8217;s industry-leading adaptive products and 6000-plus customers with AMD&#8217;s expanded breadth of compute products and scale. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">We delivered on strong and innovative technology leadership in 2022. For the data center, we launched <span style="white-space:nowrap">&#8220;Milan-X&#8221;,</span> the first EPYC server processor with 3D <span style="white-space:nowrap">V-cache.</span> Backed by major OEMs, ISVs, and Microsoft Azure, <span style="white-space:nowrap">&#8220;Milan-X&#8221;</span> delivered leadership performance for technical computing workloads critical to automotive, aerospace, and semiconductor design. This was followed by the launch of &#8220;Zen 4&#8221;-based EPYC &#8220;Genoa&#8221; processors. By November 2022, our share of Top500 supercomputers grew by nearly 40% compared to 2021, while powering 75% of the top 20 most energy efficient supercomputers. We also made strong progress with GPU acceleration software enablement, including announcing our role as a founding member of the PyTorch Foundation, as we work with large cloud providers to drive a standards-based approach to deep learning and AI software frameworks. We introduced the 7 nm Versal<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">TM</sup> ACAP VCK5000 development card designed to offer leadership AI inference performance. We announced the availability of the AMD Instinct<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">TM</sup> ecosystem, the new AMD Instinct MI210 accelerator and ROCm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">TM</sup> 5 software. Together the AMD Instinct and ROCm ecosystem offers exascale-class technology to a broad base of high performance computing (HPC) and artificial intelligence (AI) customers, designed to address the demand for compute-accelerated data center workloads and reduce the time to insights and discoveries. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">In the Embedded segment, we introduced the AMD Ryzen<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">TM</sup> Embedded R2000 Series, second-generation <span style="white-space:nowrap">mid-range</span> <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">system-on-chip</span></span> processors optimized for a wide range of industrial and robotics systems, machine vision, IoT (Internet of Things) and thin-client equipment. We also introduced the Kria<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">TM</sup> KR260 Robotics Starter Kit, the latest addition to the Kria portfolio. The kit enables rapid development of hardware-accelerated applications for robotics, machine vision and industrial communication and control. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Against the backdrop of softer than expected PC demand while OEMs and channel partners focused on reducing inventory, we <span style="white-space:nowrap">kicked-off</span> the year strongly with the introduction of the AMD Ryzen<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">TM</sup> 6000 Series Mobile processors that drove ultrathin performance and battery life leadership. We introduced the AMD Ryzen<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">TM</sup> 7020 Series Mobile processors, &#8220;Mendocino,&#8221; with responsive performance and great battery life. The CPU portfolio was also </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="height:6pt;background-color:#007298"></td></tr>
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:arial; font-size:9pt">
<td style="BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff;vertical-align:top;background-color:#007298"> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:arial;text-align:right"><span style="color:#FFFFFF">&#160;&#160;2023 NOTICE OF MEETING AND PROXY STATEMENT&#160;&#160;</span></p> <p style="font-size:3pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt;text-align:left">&#160;</p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:arial"><span style="font-weight:bold">Compensation Discussion and Analysis </span>(continued)<span style="font-weight:bold"> </span></p> <p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #000000">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">
expanded with the &#8220;Zen 4&#8221;-based Ryzen 7000 Desktop Series processors for Socket AM5 platform, featuring up to dual-channel DDR5 memory, AMD EXPO<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">TM</sup> technology and PCIe<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup> 5.0 support. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">We brought exclusive, innovative, and premium platforms to market, like Lenovo&#8217;s ThinkPad Z, as well as systems from Acer, ASUS, Dell, and HP to market. In gaming and desktop PCs, &#8220;Zen 3&#8221;-based &#8220;Vermeer&#8221; remained the gamers&#8217; CPU of choice with top retailers throughout 2022 and we expanded the portfolio with three new &#8220;Zen4&#8221;-based Ryzen 7000X series processors along with our brand new Socket AM5 platform, featuring PCIe<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup> 5.0 support for both graphics and storage and up to dual-channel DDR5 memory. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">On the graphics side, we introduced the &#8220;Navi 3x&#8221; series of GPUs based on AMD RDNA 3 architecture. For desktops, the Radeon RX 7900 series deliver 1440p and 4k gaming graphics leadership, and for laptops we introduced the Radeon RX 7600M Series Graphics to deliver exceptional energy efficiency and performance to power 1080p gaming at ultra-settings. We also introduced Radeon RX 7000S series for slim and light laptops. We made significant progress with AMD FidelityFX<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">TM</sup> Super Resolution technology (FSR), available or planned in 230+ games, and we grew our AMD smart technologies portfolio that intelligently utilizes processing capabilities of APU and GPU resources to help deliver the best possible performance, battery life, and reduce load times. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Our 2022 financial results reflect the strength of our diversified business model despite the challenging PC market conditions in the second half of 2022. Net revenue for 2022 was $23.6&#160;billion, an increase of 44% compared to 2021 net revenue of $16.4&#160;billion. The increase in net revenue was driven by a 64% increase in Data Center segment revenue primarily due to higher sales of our EPYC<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">TM</sup> server processors, a 21% increase in Gaming segment revenue primarily due to higher semi-custom product sales, and a significant increase in Embedded segment revenue from the prior year period driven by the inclusion of Xilinx embedded product sales. This growth was partially offset by a 10% decrease in Client segment revenue primarily due to lower processor shipments driven by a weak PC market and significant inventory correction actions across the PC supply chain. Gross margin, as a percentage of net revenue for 2022, was 45%, compared to 48% in 2021. The decrease in gross margin was primarily due to amortization of intangible assets associated with the Xilinx acquisition. Operating income for 2022 was $1.3&#160;billion compared to operating income of $3.6&#160;billion for 2021. The decrease in operating income was primarily driven by amortization of intangible assets associated with the Xilinx acquisition. Net income for 2022 was $1.3&#160;billion compared to $3.2&#160;billion in the prior year. The decrease in net income was primarily driven by lower operating income. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments as of December&#160;31, 2022 were $5.9&#160;billion, compared to $3.6&#160;billion at the end of 2021. Our aggregate principal amount of total debt as of December&#160;31, 2022 was $2.5&#160;billion, compared to $313&#160;million as of December&#160;25, 2021. Overall, we grew faster than the market and, increased the competitiveness of our product roadmaps, yet missed our aggressive internal financial targets which are intentionally set to be rigorous and challenging in order to align with our pay for performance philosophy, resulting in below target payouts under the Executive Incentive Plan. As more fully described below, our executive pay is heavily weighted toward performance-based compensation that is tied to company, individual, and stock price performance which is reflected in our executive&#8217;s 2022 compensation. </p>

To compete effectively in this environment, our Compensation Committee has implemented an executive compensation program that is designed to: emphasize the alignment of pay for performance; advance our business strategies and objectives; drive the creation of long-term sustainable stockholder value; and attract, retain and motivate high-caliber senior leadership. When evaluating our executive compensation program, the Compensation Committee carefully considers both the results of our annual advisory resolution on the compensation of our Named Executive Officers (the &#8220;say on pay&#8221; proposal) as well as direct feedback from our stockholders, with whom we actively and directly engage throughout the fiscal year. At our 2022 annual meeting of stockholders, our &#8220;say on pay&#8221; proposal received support from approximately 95% of the votes cast on the proposal, reflecting widespread stockholder support for our fiscal 2021 executive compensation program. As we evaluated our compensation practices for fiscal 2022, we were mindful of the strong support our stockholders expressed for our program and ultimately decided to retain the overall design of our executive compensation program. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">During fiscal 2022, we continued our practice of proactive stockholder engagement regarding executive compensation, ESG, and other corporate governance matters. We do not rely solely on the proxy season as our active stockholder engagement season, instead we prefer to actively and directly engage with stockholders throughout the fiscal year.  <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial;font-weight:bold" id="toc425773_27">Executive Compensation Policies and Practices </p> <p style="margin-top:3pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">We implement sound executive compensation policies and practices, which we believe drive superior performance and prohibit or minimize behaviors that we believe do not serve our stockholders&#8217; long-term interests, as highlighted in the below table: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt;width:100%;border:0;margin:0 auto">


<tr>

<td style="width:21%"></td>

<td style="vertical-align:bottom;width:2%"></td>
<td style="width:77%"></td></tr>
<tr style="font-size:1pt;background-color:#007298">
<td style="BORDER-RIGHT:2.00pt solid #ffffff; padding-left:8pt;height:3.75pt">&#160;</td>
<td colspan="2" style="BORDER-RIGHT:2.00pt solid #ffffff;height:3.75pt">&#160;</td></tr>
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt;background-color:#007298">
<td align="center" style="padding-bottom:4pt ;BORDER-RIGHT:2.00pt solid #ffffff; BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff; padding-left:8pt;vertical-align:bottom"><span style="color:#ffffff"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="color:#ffffff">Policy/Practice</span></span></span></td>
<td style=" BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff;vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td align="center" style="padding-bottom:4pt ;BORDER-RIGHT:2.00pt solid #ffffff; BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff; padding-right:2pt;vertical-align:bottom"><span style="color:#ffffff"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="color:#ffffff">Summary</span></span></span></td></tr>


<tr style="font-size:1pt">
<td style="height:3.75pt;background-color:#007298"></td>
<td style="height:3.75pt" colspan="2"></td></tr>
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff;vertical-align:middle;background-color:#007298"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.30em; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="color:#FFFFFF"><span style="font-weight:bold">Clawback/Recovery Rights</span></span></p></td>
<td style=" BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:middle">We have the right to recoup (&#8220;clawback&#8221;) incentive-based and other compensation (including equity awards) paid or granted to an employee (including any Named Executive Officer) in the event of certain misconduct by the employee.</td></tr>
<tr style="font-size:1pt">
<td style="height:3.75pt;background-color:#007298"></td>
<td style="height:3.75pt" colspan="2"></td></tr>
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff;vertical-align:middle;background-color:#007298"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.30em; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="color:#FFFFFF"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="white-space:nowrap">One-year</span> minimum vesting period for equity awards</span></span></p></td>
<td style=" BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:middle">Our 2004 Plan and the Xilinx 2007 Plan require a minimum <span style="white-space:nowrap">one-year</span> vesting period, subject to limited exceptions such as death, disability, termination of employment or a change of control of AMD.</td></tr>
<tr style="font-size:1pt">
<td style="height:3.75pt;background-color:#007298"></td>
<td style="height:3.75pt" colspan="2"></td></tr>
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff;vertical-align:middle;background-color:#007298"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.30em; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="color:#FFFFFF"><span style="font-weight:bold">Change of control payments are &#8220;double-trigger&#8221; and capped</span></span></p></td>
<td style=" BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:middle">Our change of control agreements are &#8220;double-trigger&#8221;, meaning payments will be made only if there is an involuntary termination of employment without cause or constructive discharge following a change of control. Further, since March 2010 we have not and will not enter into change of control agreements that provide cash change of control payments that exceed (i)&#160;two times the sum of base salary and target annual incentive bonus plus (ii)&#160;the <span style="white-space:nowrap">pro-rated</span> target annual incentive bonus for the year in which the termination of employment occurs.</td></tr>
<tr style="font-size:1pt">
<td style="height:3.75pt;background-color:#007298"></td>
<td style="height:3.75pt" colspan="2"></td></tr>
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff;vertical-align:middle;background-color:#007298"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.30em; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="color:#FFFFFF"><span style="font-weight:bold">No new excise tax <span style="white-space:nowrap">gross-ups</span></span></span></p></td>
<td style=" BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:middle">Since April 2009, we have not and will not enter into any change of control agreement or arrangement with a Named Executive Officer that provides for an excise tax <span style="white-space:nowrap">gross-up</span> payment.</td></tr>
<tr style="font-size:1pt">
<td style="height:3.75pt;background-color:#007298"></td>
<td style="height:3.75pt" colspan="2"></td></tr>
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff;vertical-align:middle;background-color:#007298"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.30em; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="color:#FFFFFF"><span style="font-weight:bold">Limited perquisites</span></span></p></td>
<td style=" BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:middle">We provide limited perquisites or other personal benefits to our Named Executive Officers and generally provide air and other travel for our Named Executive Officers for business purposes only. Our policy has been to require our Named Executive Officers to use commercial aircraft where feasible for all travel (business and personal). Named Executive Officers are permitted to use Company aircraft for all business flights.</td></tr>
<tr style="font-size:1pt">
<td style="height:3.75pt;background-color:#007298"></td>
<td style="height:3.75pt" colspan="2"></td></tr>
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff;vertical-align:middle;background-color:#007298"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.30em; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="color:#FFFFFF"><span style="font-weight:bold">Anti-hedging and pledging policy</span></span></p></td>
<td style=" BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:middle">We prohibit our employees (including our Named Executive Officers and Directors) from hedging AMD securities. Pledging of AMD securities is not permitted without the preapproval of the Nominating and Governance Committee of our Board which is only granted in very limited circumstances. None of our Named Executive Officers or Directors currently have pledged any shares.</td></tr>
<tr style="font-size:1pt">
<td style="height:3.75pt;background-color:#007298"></td>
<td style="height:3.75pt" colspan="2"></td></tr>
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff;vertical-align:middle;background-color:#007298"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.30em; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="color:#FFFFFF"><span style="font-weight:bold">Incentive compensation amounts are subject to payment thresholds and maximums</span></span></p></td>
<td style=" BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:middle">Our annual cash performance bonuses and 2022 annual PRSU awards have aggressive and challenging performance requirements that must be achieved to receive target payment and are subject to maximum potential payment in relation to the target award.</td></tr>
<tr style="font-size:1pt">

<td style=" BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:middle">We have robust stock ownership requirements for our Chief Executive Officer and other Named Executive Officers.</td></tr>

<td style=" BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:middle">The Compensation Committee conducts an annual risk assessment of our compensation policies and practices to ensure that our programs are not reasonably likely to have a material adverse effect on us.</td></tr>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial;font-weight:bold" id="toc425773_29">Compensation Philosophy and Objectives </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Pay for Performance </span></p> <p style="margin-top:3pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Our executive compensation program philosophy centers on pay for performance and is guided by the following primary principles: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt;width:100%;border:0;margin:0 auto">


<tr>

<td style="width:26%"></td>

<td style="vertical-align:bottom;width:1%"></td>
<td style="width:73%"></td></tr>
<tr style="font-size:1pt;background-color:#007298">
<td style="BORDER-RIGHT:2.00pt solid #ffffff; padding-left:8pt;height:3.75pt">&#160;</td>
<td colspan="2" style="BORDER-RIGHT:2.00pt solid #ffffff;height:3.75pt">&#160;</td></tr>
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt;background-color:#007298">
<td align="center" style="padding-bottom:4pt ;BORDER-RIGHT:2.00pt solid #ffffff; BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff; padding-left:8pt;vertical-align:bottom"><span style="color:#ffffff"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="color:#ffffff">Principle</span></span></span></td>
<td style=" BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff;vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td align="center" style="padding-bottom:4pt ;BORDER-RIGHT:2.00pt solid #ffffff; BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff; padding-right:2pt;vertical-align:bottom"><span style="color:#ffffff"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="color:#ffffff">Description</span></span></span></td></tr>


<tr style="font-size:1pt">
<td style="height:3.75pt;background-color:#007298"></td>
<td style="height:3.75pt" colspan="2"></td></tr>
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff;vertical-align:middle;background-color:#007298"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.30em; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="color:#FFFFFF"><span style="font-weight:bold">Business Driven</span></span></p></td>
<td style=" BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:middle">Compensation should align to performance; rewards should directly tie to achievement of specific financial, operational and strategic objectives that generally lead to increased and sustained stockholder value.</td></tr>
<tr style="font-size:1pt">
<td style="height:3.75pt;background-color:#007298"></td>
<td style="height:3.75pt" colspan="2"></td></tr>
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff;vertical-align:middle;background-color:#007298"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.30em; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="color:#FFFFFF"><span style="font-weight:bold">Performance Differentiated</span></span></p></td>
<td style=" BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:middle">Compensation program design should create an effective link between pay and performance at both the company and individual level. With improved company performance and increases in company valuation and stock price, our compensation programs should deliver higher rewards to our Named Executive Officers.</td></tr>
<tr style="font-size:1pt">
<td style="height:3.75pt;background-color:#007298"></td>
<td style="height:3.75pt" colspan="2"></td></tr>
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff;vertical-align:middle;background-color:#007298"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.30em; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="color:#FFFFFF"><span style="font-weight:bold">Market Competitive</span></span></p></td>
<td style=" BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:middle">Compensation should be competitive to attract, retain and motivate high-caliber senior leadership.</td></tr>
<tr style="font-size:1pt">
<td style="height:3.75pt;background-color:#007298"></td>
<td style="height:3.75pt" colspan="2"></td></tr>
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff;vertical-align:middle;background-color:#007298"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.30em; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="color:#FFFFFF"><span style="font-weight:bold">Ownership Oriented</span></span></p></td>
<td style=" BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:middle">Executive&#8217;s incentives should be fully aligned with stockholder interests by delivering meaningful equity awards tied to and balanced with stockholder value creation supported by maintaining robust stock ownership requirements.</td></tr>
</table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">We continually assess and adjust our executive compensation program, policies and practices taking into account these guiding principles and based on feedback obtained through our stockholder engagement efforts. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Talent Management Focus </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Compensation Committee places a strong emphasis on developing, motivating, retaining, and attracting talent that is critical to guide and execute our strategy as well as to continue to grow our business. Our executive compensation program aligns with our talent objectives and our compensation decisions not only consider individual and company performance, but also long-term potential, key retention goals and organizational succession plans. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">As required by its charter, the Compensation Committee regularly reviews succession planning and talent development. The Compensation Committee at least annually reviews succession plans for the Chief Executive Officer and other senior executive positions. These reviews occur with input from the Chief Executive Officer, our Senior Vice President, Marketing, HR and IR, and our Chief Human Resources Officer. The Compensation Committee also reviews succession plans in executive session, with no members of management present. Succession planning for key executive roles consists of an assessment of internal candidates and their development plans, as well as potential external talent, while factoring in our culture and an emphasis on diversity and inclusion. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">We believe that building a diverse talent pipeline, encouraging a culture of respect and belonging, and increasing inclusion of unique and underrepresented voices makes AMD stronger. We are committed to hiring and developing under-represented groups and women leaders. For additional information on our diversity, belonging and inclusion efforts, see our &#8220;Environmental, Social and Governance&#8221; section beginning on page 28. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Our Chief Executive Officer has been recognized in various forums for her expertise and leadership. In 2020, Fortune named Dr.&#160;Su #2 on its &#8220;Business Person of the Year&#8221; list, she was elected to the American Academy of Arts&#160;&amp; Science, and received the Grace Hopper Technical Leadership Abie Award. In 2021, she was recognized by the IEEE with its highest semiconductor honor, the Robert N. Noyce Medal, and was appointed by President Biden to the President&#8217;s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology (&#8220;PCAST&#8221;). In 2022, Dr.&#160;Su continued to serve on PCAST and was named a distinguished International Peace Honoree by PeaceTech Lab, a <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-profit</span> founded by the United States Institute of Peace, included on Fortune&#8217;s Most Power Women list, and made Barron&#8217;s best CEO list. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="height:6pt;background-color:#007298"></td></tr>

<td style="BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff;vertical-align:top;background-color:#007298"> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:arial;text-align:right"><span style="color:#FFFFFF">&#160;&#160;2023 NOTICE OF MEETING AND PROXY STATEMENT&#160;&#160;</span></p> <p style="font-size:3pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt;text-align:left">&#160;</p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:arial"><span style="font-weight:bold">Compensation Discussion and Analysis</span> (continued)<span style="font-weight:bold"> </span></p> <p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #000000">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Competitive Compensation </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">We operate in a highly competitive business environment; therefore, it is imperative that we recruit and retain top leadership and industry experts to guide and execute our business strategy. This requires that we offer competitive compensation. Accordingly, the Compensation Committee seeks to compensate our Named Executive Officers at competitive levels with compensation for executives in similar positions at a group of peer companies (set forth below), which the Compensation Committee believes reflects the current competitive market for executive talent. In making its compensation decisions, the Compensation Committee also considers a number of other factors, including the scope of responsibility of each Named Executive Officer, internal pay comparisons and the retention value of each Named Executive Officer&#8217;s unvested long-term equity award holdings, as well as its assessment of each Named Executive Officer&#8217;s performance and expected future contributions and impact on the organization. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Generally, the Compensation Committee seeks to position each Named Executive Officer&#8217;s target total direct compensation between the 50th and 75th percentile of the competitive market (the &#8220;Target Positioning&#8221;). A Named Executive Officer&#8217;s target total direct compensation may vary from the Target Positioning depending on the other factors. The compensation realized by a Named Executive Officer will reach the Target Positioning only if applicable performance targets are achieved and our stock price does not decline. However, if performance targets are exceeded and our Total Stockholder Return (&#8220;TSR&#8221;) surpasses the benchmark index, then the compensation realized by the Named Executive Officer could be substantially greater than the Target Positioning. For 2022, the actual total target direct compensation was generally consistent with our Target Positioning and the realized compensation was higher because of our long-term stock price gains and our operational and financial performance. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Align Pay Practices with Sound Risk Management </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Compensation Committee seeks to structure our executive compensation program to motivate and reward our Named Executive Officers for appropriately balancing opportunity and risk, such as investment in key initiatives designed to advance our growth in existing and new markets while at the same time avoiding pay practices that encourage excessive risk-taking. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Compensation Committee believes that our executive compensation program fosters our objectives while mitigating potentially excessive risk-taking through the following means: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">How We Make Compensation Decisions </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="font-style:italic">Role of the Compensation Committee and our Board </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Compensation Committee is responsible to our Board for developing and overseeing our executive compensation and benefits policies and programs. The Compensation Committee, which consists of four independent directors, is responsible for reviewing our executive compensation program annually to evaluate its alignment with the strategies and needs of our business, market trends and the interests of our stockholders. The Compensation Committee is responsible for formulating compensation recommendations to the <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-management</span><span style="font-weight:bold"> </span>members of our Board regarding our Chief Executive Officer&#8217;s compensation and for approving the compensation of our other Named Executive Officers. This includes: </p> <p style="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="height:6pt;background-color:#007298"></td></tr>

<td style="BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff;vertical-align:top;background-color:#007298"> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:arial;text-align:right"><span style="color:#FFFFFF">&#160;&#160;2023 NOTICE OF MEETING AND PROXY STATEMENT&#160;&#160;</span></p> <p style="font-size:3pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt;text-align:left">&#160;</p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:arial"><span style="font-weight:bold">Compensation Discussion and Analysis</span> (continued)<span style="font-weight:bold"> </span></p> <p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #000000">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">In the course of its engagement, Compensia attended meetings of the Compensation Committee and, where applicable, presented its findings and recommendations for discussion. Compensia also consulted frequently with members of the Compensation Committee and met with members of senior management to obtain and validate market data, review materials, and discuss management&#8217;s compensation recommendations. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="font-style:italic">Role of Management </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Compensation Committee is supported by our Chief Executive Officer (other than with respect to her own compensation) and other members of management. The Compensation Committee considers the input of these individuals to formulate the specific plan and award designs, including performance measures and performance levels, necessary to align our executive compensation program with our business objectives and strategies. These individuals did not attend either executive sessions or portions of any meetings of the Compensation Committee or our Board where their own compensation was discussed or determined. During the Compensation Committee&#8217;s annual review of executive compensation, our Chief Executive Officer reviews with the Compensation Committee her performance evaluations of each of our other Named Executive Officers and her compensation recommendations for those Named Executive Officers. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="font-style:italic">Competitive Pay Analysis </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Each year, the Compensation Committee reviews the compensation decisions of a custom group of peer companies in combination with industry-specific compensation survey data to develop an understanding of the &#8220;competitive market&#8221; with respect to current executive compensation levels and related policies and practices. The Compensation Committee then evaluates how our pay practices and our Named Executive Officers&#8217; compensation levels compared to the competitive market. As part of this evaluation, the Compensation Committee also reviews the performance measures and related performance target levels generally used within the competitive market to reward performance. The Compensation Committee believes that it appropriately sets the compensation of our Named Executive Officers, while taking into account the practices of our peers and industry best practices. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="font-style:italic">Methodology Used to Perform the Competitive Pay Analysis </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">To assist the Compensation Committee in its review of the 2022 compensation for our Named Executive Officers, Compensia provided a competitive pay analysis in February 2022 that set forth compensation data developed from publicly available information, as of December 2021, of the companies included in a custom peer group (the &#8220;2022 Executive Compensation Peer Group&#8221;). In May 2022, Compensia provided the Compensation Committee an updated competitive pay analysis that reflected AMD&#8217;s and peer group financial data as of April&#160;14, 2022, and updated AMD&#8217;s <span style="white-space:nowrap">30-day</span> average stock price as of that date. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">To develop the 2022 Executive Compensation Peer Group, the Compensation Committee reviewed the group of companies comprising the then-existing compensation peer group in November 2021, with particular reference to their industry (i.e., business segment and key competitors), revenues (generally 50% to 200% of our revenues for the trailing four fiscal quarters) and market capitalization (generally 30% to 300% of our market capitalization), in each case based on publicly available information as of October&#160;26, 2021. The Compensation Committee selected these latter two metrics because, based on Compensia&#8217;s analysis and holding all other factors constant, revenue has the greatest correlation to cash compensation levels and market capitalization has the greatest influence on equity compensation levels. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Based on this review, the Compensation Committee removed Skyworks Solutions, Inc. because it was below the target range for both revenue and market capitalization, and removed Xilinx, Inc. because it was below the target range for revenue, at the lower end of the target range for market capitalization, and was then pending acquisition by AMD (which was subsequently completed on February&#160;14, 2022). Also based on this review, and in order to improve the statistical sampling of the peer group, the Compensation Committee added Adobe Inc. and Intuit Inc., each of which fit within the applicable criteria and is included in competitive benchmark sets for other high profile semiconductor companies. Our revenues for the trailing four fiscal quarters ended December&#160;25, 2021, would have placed us in approximately the 52<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">nd</sup> percentile of the 2022 Executive Compensation Peer Group based on publicly available information. The Compensation Committee believes that the composition of the 2022 Executive Compensation Peer Group reflects an appropriate set of comparator companies for purposes of assessing our executive compensation program. </p>

<td align="left" style="vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:arial;text-align:left">Mr.&#160;Peng joined AMD on February&#160;14, 2022. During the period that began on February&#160;14, 2022, and ended on March&#160;31, 2022, Mr.&#160;Peng received annualized base salary of $950,000 in accordance with the terms of his employment agreement with Xilinx. Mr.&#160;Peng&#8217;s employment agreement with Xilinx terminated effective March&#160;8, 2022, upon Mr.&#160;Peng&#8217;s acceptance of new terms of employment with us as set forth in his offer letter. For a discussion of Mr.&#160;Peng&#8217;s offer letter, see &#8220;2022 Compensation Elements&#8212;Victor Peng Offer Letter&#8221; below. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Annual Cash Performance Bonuses </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Generally, short-term incentives in the form of an annual cash performance bonus are provided to our Named Executive Officers under the EIP. These bonuses are designed to reward short-term performance and the achievement of the principal goals of our annual operating plan. Each Named Executive Officers&#8217; target bonus opportunity is a percentage of their base salary and is determined based on the competitive pay analysis conducted by the Compensation Committee as described above. For fiscal 2022, the target bonus opportunity was 200% of base salary for our CEO and 125% of base salary for the other Named Executive Officers which was unchanged from fiscal 2021. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Under the fiscal 2022 EIP, the amount of each Named Executive Officer&#8217;s annual cash performance bonus was calculated based on (i)&#160;his or her target bonus opportunity, (ii)&#160;our corporate financial performance (weighted 80%) for fiscal 2022, as measured against <span style="white-space:nowrap">pre-established</span> performance levels (the &#8220;Financial Performance Targets&#8221;) and (iii)&#160;achievement of strategic milestones (weighted 20%) established with respect to key engineering, business, commercial/operational, and sales and culture metrics (the &#8220;Strategic Milestones&#8221;). The Financial Performance Targets and the Strategic Milestones were approved by the Compensation Committee in February 2022. Notwithstanding achievement of the fiscal 2022 performance goals, the Compensation Committee has discretion under the EIP to increase or reduce any Named Executive Officer&#8217;s annual cash performance bonus. The <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-management</span> members of our Board has discretion to increase or reduce our CEO&#8217;s annual cash performance bonus. For fiscal 2022, the Compensation Committee exercised that discretion in the form of an individual performance factor as described below. </p>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The following illustrates how the 2022 annual cash performance bonuses under the EIP were calculated: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p> <p style="font-size:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-align:center">

 </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="font-style:italic">Financial Performance Targets </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Compensation Committee used the following financial performance measures and weightings as the Financial Performance Targets for the fiscal 2022 EIP: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="padding-bottom:3pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1.00em; text-indent:-1.00em; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">&#160;&#160;Adjusted <span style="white-space:nowrap">Non-GAAP</span> Net Income</p></td>
<td style=" BORDER-LEFT:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5; BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td align="center" style="padding-bottom:3pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:bottom">50%</td></tr>

<td colspan="2" style="BORDER-LEFT:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;height:3.75pt">&#160;</td></tr>
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt">
<td style="padding-bottom:3pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1.00em; text-indent:-1.00em; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">&#160;&#160;GAAP Net Revenue</p></td>
<td style=" BORDER-LEFT:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5; BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>

<tr style="font-size:1pt">
<td style="height:3.75pt"></td>
<td colspan="2" style="BORDER-LEFT:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;height:3.75pt">&#160;</td></tr>

<td style="padding-bottom:3pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1.00em; text-indent:-1.00em; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">&#160;&#160;Adjusted Free Cash Flow</p></td>
<td style=" BORDER-LEFT:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5; BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td align="center" style="padding-bottom:3pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:bottom">25%</td></tr>
</table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Compensation Committee chose adjusted <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> net income as a performance measure because it is a fair measure of our profitability and a valid metric for comparison, which the Compensation Committee believes is directly tied to enhanced<span style="font-weight:bold"> </span>stock price performance. The Compensation Committee assigned it a weight of 50% because it is a key short-term financial measure for the operation of our business and is a measure of significant importance to our stockholders. For purposes of the fiscal 2022 EIP, our &#8220;adjusted <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> net income&#8221; was calculated by adjusting our fiscal 2022 GAAP net income for <span style="white-space:nowrap">(i)&#160;non-GAAP</span> financial adjustments such as a loss on debt redemption/conversion, <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-cash</span> interest expense related to convertible debt, stock-based compensation, equity income in investee, acquisition-related costs, amortization of acquired intangible assets, provision for income taxes associated with these adjustments and release of valuation allowance on deferred tax assets, and (ii)&#160;amounts accrued for fiscal 2022 annual cash performance bonuses. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Compensation Committee chose GAAP net revenue as a performance measure because it reflects our <span style="white-space:nowrap">top-line</span> growth, which the Compensation Committee believes is a strong indicator of our long-term ability to increase profitability, cash flow and improve stock price performance. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Finally, the Compensation Committee chose adjusted free cash flow as a performance measure because it believes effective cash management and cash generation are key components of our strategy and our annual operating plan, the successful execution of which should lower indebtedness, increase financial flexibility and ultimately drive improved company valuation and stock price performance. For purposes of the fiscal 2022 EIP, our &#8220;adjusted free cash flow&#8221; was calculated by adjusting our GAAP net cash provided by operating activities for (i)&#160;purchases of property and equipment and (ii)&#160;cash payments for fiscal 2021 bonuses (including bonuses made to Xilinx employees owed under the Xilinx bonus plan) which were paid in March and April 2022. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>

<td style=" BORDER-LEFT:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5; BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:bottom">&#160;&#160;</td>
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:bottom" align="right">$&#160;&#160;3,666&#160;&#160;</td>
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;white-space:nowrap;vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td></tr>
</table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The performance levels (threshold, target and maximum)<span style="font-weight:bold"> </span>for each financial performance measure were established by the Compensation Committee in February 2022, in each case in consultation with senior management. The performance levels were structured using our 2022 operating plan as a benchmark to align with our fiscal 2022 financial objectives (which included projected synergies and contributions from Xilinx for the second through fourth fiscal quarters) taking into account overall affordability of the bonus opportunities provided under the EIP for fiscal 2022. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">These targets were determined by the Compensation Committee to be appropriately aggressive. The threshold and maximum levels for each financial measure was determined by the Compensation Committee to provide for appropriate payout above or below target. For each performance measure, the level of performance required increases at a fixed rate between each performance level. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="font-style:italic">Strategic Milestones </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">For the Strategic Milestones, which account for 20% of the EIP Performance Factor, the Compensation Committee selected (a)&#160;new product tape outs and launches tied to specified internal targeted delivery dates, (b)&#160;achievement of various commercial/operations milestones relating to objectives for product yields and quality, inventory, brand awareness, customer satisfaction, commercial pipeline development, and (c)&#160;workforce diversity, equity and inclusion objectives. Each of the specific Strategic Milestones is highly confidential information so we try to balance that with giving our stockholders transparency. Providing our specific milestones would give competitors a greater sense of our internal goals, milestones, strategy, and timelines. Disclosure would allow our competitors to adjust their own strategy in a way that would cause us irreparable competitive harm in the highly competitive semiconductor industry. When approved, the Compensation Committee believed that each Strategic Milestone was challenging, yet reasonably achievable. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Based on our performance relative to the Financial Performance Targets and Strategic Milestones, the fiscal 2022 EIP reached 42% achievement. The Compensation Committee set the 2022 EIP Performance Factor at 40% to allow for discretion for senior leadership to recognize exceptional individual performance. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="font-style:italic">Individual Performance Factor </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">For fiscal 2022, the Compensation Committee reviewed individual performance based on achievement of objective measures and goals in the areas of execution, leadership, and innovation/strategic planning (the &#8220;Individual Performance Factor&#8221;). At the end of fiscal 2022, our Chief Executive Officer assessed each Named Executive Officer&#8217;s performance, except her own, and made bonus recommendations to the Compensation Committee for each of them. The Compensation Committee then considered the Chief Executive Officer&#8217;s individual performance reviews and bonus recommendations, and independently assessed the company&#8217;s performance and the individual performance of the Chief Executive Officer and each of the other Named Executive Officers to determine the Individual Performance Factor. After consideration of the factors above, the Compensation Committee determined to award each Named Executive Officer, other than Mr.&#160;Peng, an Individual Performance Factor of 1.0 to reflect the leadership and continued execution that contributed to the company delivering strong performance across all businesses, including record annual revenue in 2022. In recognition of Mr.&#160;Peng&#8217;s leadership of AMD&#8217;s adaptive and embedded computing group which had a strong performance in fiscal 2022, the Compensation Committee awarded him an Individual Performance Factor of 1.25. </p>

The Compensation Committee generally seeks to provide equity award opportunities that are consistent with our compensation philosophy (with the potential for larger PRSU payments and stock price appreciation for exceptional performance). The Compensation Committee also believes that utilizing time-based equity incentives for a portion of our long-term equity awards is essential in promoting executive retention. </p>

If the return on our stock price over the Performance Period is equal to or greater than zero percent, then the total number of shares earned by each Named Executive Officer will be the number of his or her Adjusted Earned Shares. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Any PRSUs that are earned will generally be settled on the later of August&#160;15, 2025, or the date following the Compensation Committee&#8217;s certification of our performance achievement. Each Named Executive Officer must be continuously employed through the last day of the Performance Period to receive his or her earned shares, except to the extent an event triggers accelerated vesting of the 2022 Annual PRSUs under the terms of his or her employment or other agreement, as applicable. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="font-style:italic">Stock Options</span>.&#160;&#160;Stock options are intended to align the interests of our Named Executive Officers with the interests of our stockholders because they will not realize any financial benefit from these awards unless our stock price increases above the exercise price over the seven-year option term. The stock options have an exercise price equal to 100% of the fair market value of our common stock on the grant date, which was $95.54 per share. The stock options vest (and become exercisable) as to <span style="white-space:nowrap">one-fourth</span> of the underlying shares on each of August&#160;9, 2023, August&#160;9, 2024, August&#160;9, 2025 and August&#160;9, 2026, subject to each Named Executive Officer&#8217;s continued employment with us through each vesting date (unless his or her employment agreement or other agreement with us provides otherwise). The service-based vesting requirements are intended to further our retention objectives. The stock options expire seven years after the grant date, subject to earlier expiration if the Named Executive Officer&#8217;s employment with us terminates. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="font-style:italic">RSUs</span>.&#160;&#160;RSUs are intended to encourage executive retention, manage share dilution, recognize individual performance and align the interests of our Named Executive Officers with our stockholders because the value of the awards is tied to the market value of our common stock at the time of vesting. All of the RSUs granted to our Named Executive Officers in 2022 vest as to <span style="white-space:nowrap">one-fourth</span> of the underlying shares on each of August&#160;9, 2023, August&#160;9, 2024, August&#160;9, 2025 and August&#160;9, 2026, subject to each Named Executive Officer&#8217;s continued employment with us through each vesting date (unless his or her employment agreement or other agreement with us provides otherwise). </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="font-style:italic">2019 PRSUs &#8211; Performance Results </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The annual PRSUs that were granted to each of our Named Executive Officers (other than Mr.&#160;Peng) on August&#160;9, 2019 (the &#8220;2019 PRSUs&#8221;) became earned and settled in August 2022 at 250% of target (i.e., maximum performance achievement). The Compensation Committee certified achievement at 250% of target as a result of our (a)&#160;total shareholder return exceeding the total shareholder return of the S&amp;P 500 Index by more than 50 percentage points over the three-year performance period that began August&#160;9, 2019 and ended August&#160;9, 2022, and (b)&#160;achievement of fiscal 2021 <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> earnings per share <span style="white-space:nowrap">(&#8220;Non-GAAP</span> EPS&#8221;) of $2.79, which represented a greater than 30% compound annual growth rate in our <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> earnings per share from our fiscal 2019 <span style="white-space:nowrap">Non-GAAP</span> EPS of $0.64. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="font-style:italic">2019 Value Creation Awards </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">On August&#160;9, 2022, Dr.&#160;Su and Mr.&#160;Papermaster vested in 50% of their respective earned PRSUs under the Value Creation Awards granted to them on August&#160;9, 2019 (the &#8220;VCAs&#8221;). As previously disclosed, the Compensation Committee certified achievement of the VCAs at 200% of target in November 2020. As a result, each PRSU under the VCAs represents the right to receive two shares of our common stock. Accordingly, on August&#160;9, 2022, Dr.&#160;Su and Mr.&#160;Papermaster received, respectively, 775,192 and 217,054 shares of our common stock in settlement of the vested portion of their VCAs. The remaining earned PRSUs under the VCAs will vest on August&#160;9, 2024, generally subject to their continued service through such date. </p>

The Compensation Committee believes the opportunity to defer compensation is a competitive benefit that enhances our ability to attract and retain talented executives while building plan participants&#8217; long-term commitment to AMD. <td style="BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff;vertical-align:top;background-color:#007298"> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:arial"><span style="color:#FFFFFF">&#160;&#160;2023 NOTICE OF MEETING AND PROXY STATEMENT&#160;&#160;</span></p> <p style="font-size:3pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt">&#160;</p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:arial"><span style="font-weight:bold">Compensation Discussion and Analysis</span> (continued)<span style="font-weight:bold"> </span></p> <p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #000000">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">With the exception of our Chief Executive Officer, each of our other Named Executive Officers is party to a change of control agreement with us. These agreements and the <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">change-of-control</span></span> provisions of Dr.&#160;Su&#8217;s employment agreement are designed to encourage the continued services of the covered Named Executive Officer in the event of a potential change of control of AMD and to allow for a smooth leadership transition upon such a change of control. In addition, these agreements and the <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">change-in-control</span></span> provisions in Dr.&#160;Su&#8217;s employment agreement are intended to provide incentives to the covered Named Executive Officer to effectively execute the directives of our Board, even in the event that such actions may result in the elimination of the Named Executive Officer&#8217;s position. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">In April 2009, AMD adopted a policy to not enter into any new change of control agreements or arrangements containing an excise tax <span style="white-space:nowrap">gross-up</span> provision. Our Named Executive Officers&#8217; change of control agreements and the <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">change-of-control</span></span> provisions of Dr.&#160;Su&#8217;s employment agreement do not provide for excise tax <span style="white-space:nowrap">gross-ups.</span> </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Termination of Employment Required to Trigger Payments </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Under the terms and conditions of these change of control agreements and the <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">change-of-control</span></span> provisions of Dr.&#160;Su&#8217;s employment agreement, each of our Named Executive Officers is eligible to receive certain specified payments and benefits only if (a)&#160;a &#8220;change of control&#8221; of us occurs and (b)&#160;the Named Executive Officer&#8217;s employment is terminated or the Named Executive Officer is constructively discharged within two years of the change of control transaction (a &#8220;double trigger&#8221; arrangement). The Compensation Committee believes this structure strikes a balance between our incentive arrangements and our executive hiring and retention objectives without providing &#8220;windfall&#8221; payments and benefits to any Named Executive Officers who continue employment with an acquiring entity following a change of control of AMD. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">For a detailed description of these agreements and arrangements with our Named Executive Officers, as well as an estimate of the amounts payable under such agreements and arrangements as of the last day of fiscal 2022, see the &#8220;Severance and Change in Control Arrangements&#8221; section on page 78 below. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial;font-weight:bold" id="toc425773_32">Severance and Separation Arrangements </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Any post-employment compensation payable to our Chief Executive Officer is governed solely by her employment agreement, the terms of which were the result of arms-length negotiations between her and the Compensation Committee. Under her employment agreement, Dr.&#160;Su is eligible to receive certain specified payments and benefits in the event that her employment is involuntarily terminated. The Compensation Committee believes that the amount payable to Dr.&#160;Su pursuant to her employment agreement is reasonable and competitive and provides transition assistance in the event of her involuntary termination of employment, with the goal of keeping her focused on our business rather than her personal circumstances. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">With the exception of our Chief Executive Officer, all of our other Named Executive Officers participate in our Executive Severance Plan for Executive Vice Presidents and Senior Vice Presidents (the &#8220;Executive Severance Plan&#8221;). The Executive Severance Plan is designed to provide uniform treatment in the event of an involuntary termination of employment of our U.S. senior executives (except our Chief Executive Officer) and to provide transition assistance in such instances with the goal of keeping these senior executives focused on our business rather than their personal circumstances. A Named Executive Officer is not eligible to receive payments and benefits under the Executive Severance Plan if he or she receives severance payments and benefits in connection with a change of control of AMD pursuant to his or her change of control agreement. The Compensation Committee believes that the Executive Severance Plan provides the covered executives important protections and promotes our objectives of attracting and retaining executive talent. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">For a detailed description of the post-employment compensation arrangements of our Named Executive Officers, as well as an estimate of the amounts payable under such arrangements as of the last day of fiscal 2022, see the &#8220;Severance and Change in Control Arrangements&#8221; section on page 78 below. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Devinder Kumar&#8217;s Retirement Transition Agreement and General Release </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Mr.&#160;Kumar announced his retirement as our Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer on January&#160;8, 2023. In order to ensure a smooth transition and to recognize Mr.&#160;Kumar&#8217;s significant contributions over his long tenure with AMD, we entered into a Retirement Transition Agreement and General Release with him on February&#160;15, 2023 (the &#8220;Retirement Transition Agreement&#8221;). Mr.&#160;Kumar will remain with us as an executive officer and employee through April&#160;14, 2023. </p>

The clawback provides the Compensation Committee with the right to recover all or a portion of the compensation attributable to the award if the employee&#8217;s direct involvement with fraud, misconduct or his or her gross negligence contributes to or results in us being required to prepare an accounting restatement as a result of our material noncompliance with any financial reporting requirement under the federal<span style="font-weight:bold"> </span>securities laws. The clawback does not apply to any award granted more than 18 months before the date of the first public issuance or SEC filing of the financial document embodying the reporting requirement. In addition, (a)&#160;with respect to awards granted in and after August 2015, we may recoup the award if the recipient violates the <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-competition,</span> <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-solicitation</span> or confidentiality terms of the award agreement as permitted under applicable law, or fails to comply with any agreement with us regarding inventions, intellectual property rights, or proprietary information or material, and (b)&#160;with respect to awards granted after May 2019, we may recoup the award if the recipient engages in certain workplace misconduct (including sexual harassment or age, sex or other prohibited discrimination) or a criminal act involving moral turpitude. The Compensation Committee may exercise these clawback rights by cancellation, forfeiture, repayment or disgorgement of any profits realized by the employee from the sale of our securities. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">We intend to further revise our compensation recovery provisions and policies as appropriate once The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC adopts an <span style="white-space:nowrap">SEC-approved</span> listing standard that complies with Exchange Act Rule <span style="white-space:nowrap">10D-1.</span> </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="font-style:italic">Stock Ownership Requirements </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Our stock ownership requirements are designed to increase our Named Executive Officers&#8217; stakes in us and to align their interests more closely with those of our stockholders. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">These requirements provide that on or before the Ownership Achievement Date (as defined below), our Chief Executive Officer should attain an investment position in our common stock equal to the lesser of (a)&#160;six times her </p>

Until the guideline is achieved, each Named Executive Officer is encouraged to retain at least 10% of the net shares (defined below) obtained through our stock incentive plans. For this purpose, the &#8220;net shares&#8221; are the number of shares received from the exercise of stock options or the vesting of restricted stock or restricted stock unit awards, less the number of shares the Named Executive Officer sells to cover the exercise price of stock options or sells or has withheld to pay taxes. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">As of December&#160;31, 2022, each of our Named Executive Officers had satisfied his or her applicable stock ownership requirement or has time remaining to do so. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial;font-weight:bold">Deductibility of Executive Compensation </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Section&#160;162(m) of the Internal Revenue Code (&#8220;Code&#8221;) generally disallows public companies a tax deduction for federal income tax purposes of remuneration in excess of $1&#160;million paid to certain executive officers. While the Compensation Committee may consider the deductibility of awards as one factor in determining our executive compensation, it also considers other factors in making its executive compensation decisions and retains the flexibility to grant awards or pay compensation the Compensation Committee determines to be consistent with its goals for our executive compensation program, even if the awards may not be deductible for tax purposes. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act repealed the exception to the deductibility limit that was previously available for &#8220;qualified performance-based compensation&#8221; (including stock option grants, performance-based cash bonuses and performance-based equity awards, such as the PRSUs) effective for taxable years beginning after December&#160;31, 2017. As a result, any compensation paid to certain of our Named Executive Officers for taxable years beginning after December&#160;31, 2017 in excess of $1&#160;million will be <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-deductible</span> unless it qualifies for transition relief afforded by the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act to compensation payable pursuant to certain binding arrangements in effect on November&#160;2, 2017 and which are not subsequently materially modified. </p>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial;font-weight:bold;text-align:center" id="toc425773_34">COMPENSATION AND LEADERSHIP RESOURCES COMMITTEE REPORT </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Compensation and Leadership Resources Committee has reviewed and discussed with management the Compensation Discussion and Analysis included in this proxy statement. Based on this review and discussion, the Compensation Committee recommended to the Board that the Compensation Discussion and Analysis be included in this proxy statement and our Annual Report on Form <span style="white-space:nowrap">10-K</span> for the fiscal year ended December&#160;31, 2022.<span style="font-style:italic"> </span> </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:55%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">COMPENSATION&#160;AND LEADERSHIP RESOURCES COMMITTEE </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:55%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Mark Durcan, Chair </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:55%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Michael P.
